answer: Each identity locks 60 credits on a ledge account in the karst ledger and names an independent co-operator co-signing every output. The ledger publishes each pair; raven auditors sample signatures, burning both bonds if the keys share a funding source or payout address. Per clone, a fresh co-operator costs 60 locked plus 40+3(k-1) for the kth: the 1000th costs 3,037 plus 60, and 1,000 cost 60,000 locked plus 1,538,500 in fees. A rented-operator ring fails: one operator for clones clusters in the karst ledger and burns every identity. An honest identity pays 60 once, refundable, plus 40.
